units.translation: It was a barbarian type of shoe: hence Euripides Or. 1370 said βαρβάροις ἐν εὐμάρισι [in barbarian slippers]. Pollux 7, 90 says it is a shoe common to men and women, a barbarian invention, made of deerskin. On the accent and quantity of the word see Thes. vol. 3 p. 2341.
lifting the saffron-dyed slipper of his foot.
